originalTitle: Who will make the bigger splash? Two blockbuster David Hockney exhibitions opening in Australia
summary: A immersive show made with the British artist before he died is headed to Sydney, at the same time as a Hockney portraiture exhibition at Canberra’s National Gallery
content: Two blockbuster exhibitions dedicated to the late David Hockney are opening in Australia later this year, months after the British artist’s death at the age of 88. The National Gallery of Australia in Canberra, home to the largest collection of Hockney’s work in Australia, will stage David Hockney: Portraits in Print from September to February. The exhibition will span more than 60 works made over 30 years and offers “an intimate view of his personal life, creative practice and deep engagement with portraiture”, the NGA said. And from October to January, Carriageworks in Sydney is staging David Hockney: Bigger & Closer (not smaller & further away), an immersive exhibition created by Lightroom London with Hockney himself, who recorded narration that guides visitors through his processes and philosophy. Bigger & Closer has been staged in London, Manchester, Shanghai and Seoul and visited by 650,000 people so far. “David is there as your favourite uncle who takes you to an art gallery and says something insightful to you over your shoulder, points something out to you in a painting you would never have caught on your own,” said Richard Slaney, the CEO of Lightroom and producer of Bigger & Closer. Sign up for a weekly email featuring our best reads Slaney wrote to Hockney to pitch the show in 2019 and continued to work with him on projects until a couple of weeks before his death in June. Hockney spent months working on the show, dedicated to the point that “we’d have to politely ask him to leave sometimes”, said Slaney. “He treated this show like an artwork in its own right, which is a real honour. He would stand there describing what had happened with particular paintings and we said, this is what we want to hear. So we went through thousands of hours of archive interviews and had him record new lines. “I’m sure people were moved by the show before he passed anyway, because hearing him explain things is just lovely. But even more so now. We’re really honoured that his studio and his family are really supportive of the show continuing out there as a legacy piece.” Hockney’s career spanned six decades. He made his name as a pop artist during the swinging 60s and was perhaps best known for his paintings of swimming pools that helped define the Los Angeles aesthetic, such as A Bigger Splash and Portrait of an Artist (Pool With Two Figures). He also produced portraits using photo-collage, experimented with abstract landscape painting and, in later life, painted works on his iPad and experimented with 3D technology. Slaney said the NGA show and the Carriageworks show, which are entirely independent of each other, will provide very different experiences for art lovers. “When we first opened, some people in the press said, why go to this when you’ve got art galleries full of Hockney paintings available? And the answer is, well, because they complement each other. This is a gateway for people into understanding his work. It’s just that the canvas is bigger and you’re closer to it – hence the title of the show. “What a life, and what a life well lived. I had the privilege to work with him for a little portion of that but everything that is written about him is absolutely true – he just wanted to work and he loved life, and the fact that he was making work until near the end was amazing.” Given his love for the aesthetics of Los Angeles, Australia was an obvious home for Hockney, Slaney said: “He was all about sunshine, light and swimming pools. He talked about Los Angeles in those terms, and obviously there are lots of similarities in terms of light, outdoors and colour, for sure.” David Hockney: Portraits in Print opens at the NGA on 5 September while David Hockney: Bigger & Closer (not smaller & further away) opens at Carriageworks on 22 October.
chineseTitle: 谁会引起更大的轰动？两场轰动一时的大卫·霍克尼展览在澳大利亚开幕
chineseSummary: 这位英国艺术家生前举办的沉浸式展览即将前往悉尼，同时堪培拉国家美术馆将举办霍克尼肖像展
chineseContent: 纪念已故大卫·霍克尼 (David Hockney) 的两场轰动一时的展览将于今年晚些时候在澳大利亚开幕，距这位英国艺术家于 88 岁去世几个月后。位于堪培拉的澳大利亚国家美术馆是澳大利亚最大的霍克尼作品收藏地，将于 9 月至 2 月举办“大卫·霍克尼：版画肖像”展览。 NGA 表示，此次展览将涵盖 30 多年来创作的 60 多件作品，“深入展示他的个人生活、创作实践和对肖像画的深入参与”。从 10 月到 1 月，悉尼的 Carriageworks 正在举办大卫·霍克尼：更大和更近（不是更小和更远），这是由 Lightroom London 与霍克尼本人共同创建的沉浸式展览，霍克尼录制了旁白，引导参观者了解他的过程和哲学。 Bigger & Closer 已在伦敦、曼彻斯特、上海和首尔上演，迄今已有 65 万人次参观。 Lightroom 首席执行官兼 Bigger & Closer 制片人理查德·斯兰尼 (Richard Slaney) 表示：“大卫就像你最喜欢的叔叔一样，带你去美术馆，在你身后对你说了一些富有洞察力的话，向你指出了一幅你自己永远无法捕捉到的画作中的东西。”订阅每周电子邮件，其中包含我们的最佳读物。斯兰尼在 2019 年写信给霍克尼宣传该剧，并继续与他合作开展项目，直到他 6 月去世前几周。霍克尼花了几个月的时间制作这部剧，致力于“有时我们不得不礼貌地请他离开”，斯兰尼说。 “他把这次展览当作一件艺术品本身，这是一种真正的荣誉。他会站在那里描述特定绘画所发生的事情，我们说，这就是我们想听到的。所以我们进行了数千小时的档案采访
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
